title: Update package.json scripts with concurrently
description: Update the npm scripts in package.json so that `npm run dev` starts both the Next.js admin app (port 3000) and the Express scraping sidecar (port 3001) simultaneously using concurrently. Also add a db:migrate script.
acceptanceCriteria: `npm run dev` starts both Next.js and Express scraping server simultaneously
Both processes log their startup messages in the terminal
`npm run build` builds only the Next.js app (scraper is not built separately)
`npm run start` starts both processes in production mode
`npm run db:migrate` runs the Drizzle migration
Killing the terminal (Ctrl+C) stops both processes

steps.details:
Update the scripts section of package.json:
```json
"scripts": {
  "dev": "concurrently \"next dev\" \"tsx src/scraper/server.ts\"",
  "build": "next build",
  "start": "concurrently \"next start\" \"tsx src/scraper/server.ts\"",
  "test": "vitest",
  "test:e2e": "playwright test",
  "db:migrate": "tsx src/db/migrate.ts"
}
```

Run `npm run dev`. Verify both 'Next.js ready' and 'Scraping API running on port 3001' messages appear in the terminal. Visit http://localhost:3000 and http://localhost:3001/api/health to confirm both are running.

technicalNotes: concurrently uses `--kill-others-on-fail` by default — if one process crashes, both stop. This is the correct behavior for dev.
In production (`npm start`), tsx compiles on-the-fly which is fine for a local tool. For a real production deploy, compile the scraper separately.
